transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-25 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~46 minutes. Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Rios (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (QuantumBridge, Head of Platform), Carlos Mendes (QuantumBridge, Security Architect), Zoë Liu (QuantumBridge, SRE Lead).

00:00 Maya Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Maya, I'm the account lead here at Redwood. We have Daniel from our SE team as well. Quick objective for today is to understand your security and deployment constraints so we can recommend Hosted, Dedicated, or Private.

00:16 Priya Nair: Hey thanks, yes we wanted to confirm scope. We're evaluating for a pilot across two products, but security is the gating factor. SOC2, key management, data retention, those are the big ones.

00:27 Daniel Rios: Great, thanks Priya. Very quick ask — could you outline current infra? are you cloud-first, GCP, multi-region needs, any air-gap requirements?

00:36 Priya Nair: We're primarily GCP with a bit in Azure for DR. No full air-gap but some workloads require VPC-only access and customer-managed keys. Also compliance team will require regular evidence for SOC2 and we do ISO planning later this year.

00:50 Carlos Mendes: To add, any solution that holds embeddings or PII needs strict retention and a documented deletion flow. We also need audit logs forwarded to our Splunk instance for 12 months, and SSO via SAML + SCIM.

01:03 Maya Chen: Understood. At a high level, we offer three modes: Hosted API — fastest to start, but for strict KMS and VPC controls Dedicated — reserved GPU pools in isolated tenancy with customer network peering Private — customer-managed control plane in your VPC or on-prem. We can walk through the controls mapped to your requirements.

01:22 Priya Nair: For Hosted, do you support bring-your-own-key?

01:25 Daniel Rios: Hosted supports managed keys by default; we do have BYOK for some enterprise tiers, but it depends on the contract and region. If full customer-managed KMS is required, Dedicated with VPC peering or Private deployment is more straightforward.

01:39 Zoë Liu: How is the KV cache handled? We can't have persistent caches storing embeddings long-term.

01:45 Daniel Rios: Good question. We have automatic prefix and KV cache eviction policies. For Dedicated and Private you can set TTLs and disable persistent caching. In Hosted we keep ephemeral caches and embeddings are not stored unless you opt into the embeddings API storage feature — that can be disabled. Note: transcripts sometimes say "K V cash" in automated notes — but it's KV cache.

02:08 Carlos Mendes: SOC2 evidence — what do you provide? Type II and scope?

02:12 Maya Chen: We can provide SOC2 Type II, audit report redacted, and a SOC2 bridge letter for recent changes. We also have ISO 27001 cert in progress; expected audit completion Q3 2026. We'll send the redacted report and a controls mapping to your INFOSEC team.

02:30 Priya Nair: Is there a public SOC2 report portal? We have procurement rules that only accept signed artifacts.

02:36 Maya Chen: We'll upload the signed redacted report into your secure SSO link. Also happy to sign an NDA for full evidence if needed.

02:45 Zoë Liu: On SSO, we need SAML + SCIM provisioning and role sync. How fine-grained is RBAC? Can we limit model access by role and environment?

02:56 Daniel Rios: RBAC supports role-based policies that map to routes and models. In Dedicated/Private you get full enterprise RBAC with custom roles, actions, and resource scoping. Hosted supports teams/orgs with pre-defined roles but limited custom role creation. You can block access to specific models and routes, and separate token scopes for read-only vs admin.

03:20 Carlos Mendes: Do audit logs capture token usage and API payloads? We can't export full payloads with PII, but we need metadata, IP, user identity, request id, model id, latency, and a hash reference for payloads.

03:34 Daniel Rios: Audit logs capture metadata (request id, user, model, timestamps, region, response codes). By default payloads are not stored in logs; we can include request/response hashes for traceability. For Dedicated/Private we can export logs to your Splunk or Cloud Logging with a retention policy you set. Hosted can stream to a SIEM with a partner connector.

04:00 Priya Nair: Data residency — can we guarantee data stays in EU for EU tenants?

04:06 Maya Chen: Yes, we have region-specific routing. For Hosted we can pin data to EU regions. Dedicated and Private offer stronger guarantees since they are physically provisioned in a region you choose. For absolute legal guarantees we recommend Private.

04:20 Carlos Mendes: KMS — we use Google Cloud KMS and we may put some keys in an HSM. How tight is the integration? We need envelope encryption in transit and at rest and the ability to rotate keys without downtime.

04:33 Daniel Rios: We support GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customer HSMs (via key wrap). For Private you can bring your own keys entirely and we never have access to plaintext keys. Key rotation workflows are supported with zero-downtime key rotation patterns; we'll share the technical note.

04:50 Priya Nair: Regarding retention, can you implement per-customer retention windows for embeddings and logs, and support on-demand deletion requests?

04:58 Daniel Rios: Yes — Dedicated and Private have per-customer retention controls, automatable via API. Hosted we can set org-level policies and an API to request deletion; SLA depends on tier. We'll include the deletion flow in the doc pack.

05:14 Carlos Mendes: Any third-party pen test results?

05:18 Maya Chen: We run annual pen tests and will provide summary findings. We don't publish full reports without an NDA but can provide highlights and remediation timelines.

05:26 Priya Nair: What about compliance for regulated data — do you restrict model families or quantization variants in Private? We tried a vendor who swapped to a smaller model for cost and that changed outputs.

05:39 Daniel Rios: You control model pinning and rollout policy in all modes. Private/Dedicated let you pin to specific model versions; we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback. Quantization profiles are configurable per-deployment.

05:56 Zoë Liu: Network — do you support private endpoints and no public internet egress for request/response?

06:02 Daniel Rios: Yes — Private supports private endpoints, no public egress, and on-prem bundles for air-gapped environments. Dedicated supports VPC peering and strict egress rules. Hosted is public by default but can be configured with private networking for higher tiers.

06:20 Priya Nair: Timelines — if we want a pilot in June, what's realistic?

06:24 Maya Chen: For a Hosted pilot it's immediate. Dedicated with reserved capacity can be provisioned in 4-6 weeks; Private can be 8-12 weeks depending on on-prem packaging and procurement.

06:36 Carlos Mendes: Procurement wants to see the full SAML metadata and SCIM example payloads.

06:42 Maya Chen: We'll attach SAML metadata, SCIM mapping examples, and an RBAC role matrix in the follow-up.

06:49 Priya Nair: Are there any known issues about model drift or quality regressions when using quantized runtimes? We need to know tradeoffs.

06:59 Daniel Rios: There are measurable differences with extreme quantization; our Optimize toolkit recommends profiles by workload and we run regression tests against your eval sets before rollout. We can run a small A/B quality check as part of the pilot.

07:14 Priya Nair: Ok seems good. Can you send a one-pager of the recommended mode for our constraints?

07:18 Maya Chen: Absolutely — we'll recommend Dedicated with VPC peering if you want BYOK and faster time to value; Private if you need full control and on-prem. We'll include a cost delta.

07:27 Zoë Liu: One last thing — retention of logs for 12 months, Splunk forwarding, and SCIM provisioning — those are must-haves.

07:32 Maya Chen: Noted. We'll also include a proposed schedule for the May SE deep dive and a benchmark window.

07:38 Priya Nair: Great thanks everyone.

07:41 Maya Chen: Thanks all. Recap of next steps: we'll send SOC2 redacted report, SAML/SCIM artifacts, Private/Dedicated checklist, and schedule the deep dive.

07:50 Meeting end.

Notes on transcript: This is an automated-ish transcription with occasional mistranscriptions (e.g., "sock two" for SOC2, "K V cash" for KV cache). Speaker attribution sometimes simplified.
